'''Kashima Shrine''' (鹿島神社, [[:en:Kyujitai|Kyujitai]]: 鹿島神社) is a type of Shinto shrine named "Kashima" dedicated to the deity Takemikazuchi.

There are approximately 600 Kashima Shrines nationwide, concentrated primarily in the Tōhoku region and the Kantō region, with the head shrine being Kashima Jingū in Kashima, Ibaraki, Ibaraki Prefecture. Most of these shrines were established by inviting the deity from Kashima Jingū, worshipping the same deity, Takemikazuchi.

Takemikazuchi, together with Futsunushi of Katori Jingū (Katori, Chiba, Chiba Prefecture), was revered by the Imperial court and central aristocracy as the ancestral deity of the Nakatomi clan and Fujiwara clan. Being a god of martial prowess, Takemikazuchi was also worshipped by samurai families ('''Kashima belief''').
